fields.meta_description: Take an eight-question color personality quiz that names your color, or build one that recommends products and saves each answer.
fields.h1: Build a Color Personality Quiz That Names Your Color
fields.hero_description: Build a color personality quiz that names a color and saves every answer, or take the eight-question quiz below.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Color Personality Quiz From Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Name your four colors and what each result shows. Emergent builds the quiz and the table behind it, and changes either when you ask.
fields.feature_1:
Every option points to a color

Name four colors in your prompt, such as Orange, Blue, Green, and Purple, and each answer option maps to one. The color picked most often wins; a tie goes to the first listed.
fields.feature_2:
A result page with a next step

The result screen names the color and what the answers lean toward, then shows the next step you chose for it: three candles from your shop or a four-swatch paint palette.
fields.feature_3:
Each finished quiz saved as a row

Every play lands in a database you own, with each pick, the color it scored, and the finish time. Filter the table by color before a sale and see exactly who landed where.
fields.feature_4:
A live count of colors in the room

Put a live chart on a second screen and watch it count each color as people finish. A facilitator projects it while the group answers on phones and opens with the real split.
fields.feature_5:
One question per phone screen

Players tap through one question per screen with a progress bar, so a link in a text or a QR code on a counter works fine. Emergent puts no cap on how many responses come in.
fields.feature_6:
Results sent where you already work

The app can post each finished result to Slack or email you the color. It can also pass a player's email through your email tool's API, onto a mailing list for that color.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places a Color Personality Quiz Runs
fields.tab_content_1:
After Ocean Blue, three candles to try

Hollow Pine Candle Co. runs the quiz on its online shop. Tessa Morgan lands on Ocean Blue, and her result page shows the three candles the owner tagged for blue. Her email joins the Ocean Blue list in the shop's email tool, and the play sits as a row in the shop's table.
fields.tab_content_2:
Forest Green and four swatches, sent to Ines

Calloway Interiors puts the quiz on its homepage. Marcus Webb finishes on Forest Green, and his result shows a four-swatch palette for green rooms. He requests a consult, and designer Ines Calloway gets a Slack message with his color and the palette he saw. The request lands beside his answers in the studio's table.
fields.tab_content_3:
Who is in the room: nine Oranges, three Purples

Dana Kowalski starts every two-day offsite with the quiz. The 24 people in the room take it on their phones, and the projector counts each color as answers land: Orange 9, Blue 7, Green 5, Purple 3. She opens the first session from that split, and every pick stays in her table for the debrief.
fields.tab_content_4:
No names, just a project per color

Mr. Okafor gives the quiz to his Grade 7 art class with no names saved. Each result opens a painting project in that color family, so a student whose color is Green starts a landscape in greens. All 27 students begin in the same period, and he sees the count per color, never who picked what.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Color Personality Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a color personality quiz where every color can win, then have Emergent build it from one prompt.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick four colors and define each one
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Point one option to each color
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose colors that read as different moods, not four shades of one family. Write a one-line meaning for each, such as Orange for bold starts or Blue for calm focus. Those lines become the first sentence of each result page.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about choices people make without thinking: the seat they take in a new room, or the first thing they unpack after a trip. Questions about habits beat asking which color someone likes. Keep it to eight so a player finishes in one sitting.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each question four options, one pointing to each color, and every color stays in play on every question. Skip options that point nowhere; they make results drift toward whichever color has the most mappings. Write the mapping down before you prompt, color by color.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write the four options at matching length, each one somebody would be glad to pick. If one option reads as the cool answer, picks pile up there and the other three colors starve. Read each set aloud and fix the option you would never choose.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Give each color its own result page
fields.howto_step_5_des: Open each page with what the answers lean toward, reusing the one-line meaning from step 1, and phrase it as a preference rather than a fixed trait. End with one next step a player can take while the result still feels true.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Prompt Emergent to build the quiz
fields.howto_step_6_des: Paste the questions and the mapping into one prompt, with a line on what each result page shows, and Emergent builds the whole thing from that description. Ask for changes in plain words, such as swapping one question's options or renaming a color.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Take it once aiming at each color
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before sharing, play four rounds, each time answering as someone who should land on one color. If a color never wins, loosen an option that points elsewhere. Check what a tie shows, and reorder the colors if the wrong one takes it.

faq_plan.q: What is a color personality quiz?
faq_plan.a: A color personality quiz is a short quiz that sorts each player into one color from their everyday choices, then tells them what their answers lean toward. The eight-question version on this page names one of four colors; a shop or a workshop builds its own to point each color at a next step.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a color personality quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in one prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: name your four colors, the questions, which option points to which color, and what each result page shows. Emergent returns the working quiz with a table recording every play, and you change any question or result by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: Should a color personality quiz ask for a favorite color?
faq_plan.hint: What is my favorite color personality quiz?
faq_plan.a: No. A favorite color question lets players steer straight to the result they expect, and the other questions stop mattering. Keep the choices indirect, such as rooms or weekend plans, and the result stays a small surprise worth sharing.

faq_plan.q: How many colors should a color personality quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Four works for a quiz of eight questions: every color can score on each question, and no result sits out of reach. Past six, options thin out and results blur together. If you want named types instead of colors, build a personality quiz and give each type its own page.

faq_plan.q: Where can I share a color personality quiz?
faq_plan.a: Anywhere a link opens: a product page, an email footer, a text to past customers, or a slide at the start of a session. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits; the quiz can live at your own address instead of a quiz platform's.

faq_plan.q: Can a group take a color personality quiz at the same time?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put one QR code on the screen and everyone plays on their own phone at once. Ask for a session field in your prompt, and each group's plays stay separate in the table, ready to compare across workshops. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: Can a color personality quiz grow an email list?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the result is worth trading an email for. Ask for the address on the last screen and say what the player gets, such as the result plus a discount code. Each address is saved in a table you own, tagged with its color. A marketing quiz runs on the same trade, whatever the topic.

faq_plan.q: Do players need an account to take a color quiz?
faq_plan.a: No. A link opens the quiz, and the result shows at the end with nothing to sign up for. Asking for an email is a separate choice: a shop building lists by color wants it, and a classroom saving no names leaves it out.

faq_plan.q: Can I change a color personality quiz after it is live?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Describe the change in a prompt and keep sharing the same link. Rows already saved stay as they were scored. On paid plans, you can export the quiz's full code to your GitHub repository and keep versions there.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse the structure of a color personality quiz for another topic?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The matching structure carries over whole: keep the questions' shape, swap the colors for dog breeds, and the same build becomes a dog breed quiz. Results change, the mapping logic stays. Write the new result pages first; the rest is renaming.

quiz.title: The Color Personality Quiz: Eight Questions to Your Color
quiz.intro: Eight quick questions about everyday choices. Answer without overthinking, and the quiz names the color your answers lean toward: Orange, Blue, Green, or Purple.

questions.text: A free Saturday with no plans lands in your lap. What happens first?

options.text: Text the group chat and get something moving
Coffee, a book, and a slow start
A long walk, then errands you have been meaning to do
Start the odd project you have been circling for weeks

questions.text: You walk into a party where you know two people. Where are you an hour later?

options.text: In the middle of the kitchen, mid-story
In a corner, deep in one good conversation
Helping the host carry things and meeting people that way
On the balcony debating something strange with a stranger

questions.text: Money aside, which vacation do you pick?

options.text: A city you have never seen, booked for next month
A quiet cabin with a lake and no signal
A trail you hike a little farther each year
A festival in a town you cannot find on a map yet

questions.text: What does your desk look like right now?

options.text: Covered in the current project, nothing else matters
Tidy, labeled, and exactly how you left it
A few plants, a few mugs, comfortable
Layers of sketches, notes, and three unfinished ideas

questions.text: A friend calls with a problem. What do they get from you?

options.text: A pep talk and a push to act today
Questions first, advice only if they ask
Soup, a ride, or whatever actually helps
A reframe that makes the problem look different

questions.text: What ruins a movie for you?

options.text: Nothing happening for the first hour
A loud crowd talking through the quiet parts
Characters nobody would ever be friends with
An ending you saw coming from the trailer

questions.text: The group project is due Friday. What is your role by Wednesday?

options.text: The one who kicked it off and set the pace
The one quietly fixing the details everyone missed
The one keeping everyone fed, calm, and on speaking terms
The one who pitched the version nobody expected
Up and out the door, plans forming on the move
The same good routine, uninterrupted
Outside early, whatever the weather
Awake at odd hours, best ideas before breakfast

results.title: Your Color Is Orange
results.description: Your answers lean toward quick starts, bright rooms, and plans that leave space for a detour. You said yes to the loud option more than once. Orange picks the new thing first and learns the details on the way. Share your color, then see which friend lands on the opposite one.

results.title: Your Color Is Blue
results.description: Your answers lean toward calm rooms, one thing at a time, and conversations that go past small talk. Blue likes depth over speed and keeps a short list of favorites instead of a long list of likes. Share your color and count how many Blues are around you.

results.title: Your Color Is Green
results.description: Your answers lean toward the outdoors, steady routines, and fixing things rather than replacing them. Green reads the room before speaking and keeps promises small enough to keep. When a group is split, the quiet workable plan is usually yours. Share your color and compare with your group.

results.title: Your Color Is Purple
results.description: Your answers lean toward the unexpected pick, the question nobody else asked, and ideas that arrive at odd hours. Purple collects interests the way other colors collect routines and would rather be surprising than tidy. Share your color and see who else landed on Purple.
